stem: What is a characteristic behavior often reported by parents of children with intermittent exotropia?

options.text: Closing one eye in bright sunlight.
Tilting the head to the shoulder when reading.
Constant crossing of the eyes when tired.
Rubbing the eyes frequently when looking at books.

explanation: Children with intermittent exotropia may close one eye in sunlight to avoid double vision as their eye starts to drift.
rationale: Consider how environmental lighting affects the child's ocular symptoms.

optionExplanations.A: Children with intermittent exotropia may close one eye in sunlight to avoid double vision as their eye starts to drift.
optionExplanations.B: Head tilts are more commonly associated with paralytic strabismus, such as fourth nerve palsy.
optionExplanations.C: Exotropia refers to the eye turning out, not crossing (esotropia).
optionExplanations.D: While common in refractive errors, this is not the specific indicator mentioned for intermittent exotropia.
